function.mechanism: Sucralose provides intense sweetness with negligible calories; chlorination of sucrose alters metabolism while preserving sweet taste receptor activation.

adi.basis: EFSA FAF Panel (2026) retained the existing ADI after re-evaluation.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA concluded no concern for genotoxicity or carcinogenicity and retained ADI 15 mg/kg bw/day; high-end exposure concerns were mainly scenario-dependent (toddlers, brand-loyal/MPL assumptions).

fda.notes: Approved food additive (not GRAS). Permitted as a sweetener in foods generally under GMP in amounts reasonably required for intended effect.

adi.basis: JECFA database lists ADI 0-15 mg/kg bw/day (Meeting 35, year 1990).

concerns.summary: Recent human trials and intervention studies reported sucralose-associated shifts in gut microbiota and glycemic-response metrics in some participants.

An in vitro study reported potential genotoxic concern for sucralose-6-acetate (an impurity/metabolite associated with sucralose), though EFSA's 2026 re-evaluation did not conclude a genotoxicity concern for sucralose itself at assessed exposures.
Animal immunology work suggests high-dose sucralose can modulate T-cell responses, with uncertain relevance to typical dietary exposure.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2026 found no concern for genotoxicity or carcinogenicity and retained ADI 15 mg/kg bw/day.
FDA continues approval under 21 CFR 172.831 with GMP-limited use.
JECFA ADI remains 0-15 mg/kg bw/day in the WHO database.

adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA reported refined exposure usually below ADI, but exceedance can occur in some toddler scenarios; conservative MPL scenarios can substantially exceed ADI in toddlers and adolescents.

risk_assessment.rationale: Major regulators continue to approve sucralose with established ADIs, but EFSA's 2026 assessment still identified scenario-dependent ADI exceedance risk in children, and recent human/mechanistic literature shows credible but not definitive metabolic and biological concern signals.
key_factors: EFSA retained ADI 15 mg/kg bw/day in 2026 and found no carcinogenic/genotoxic concern at assessed exposures.
FDA regulates sucralose as an approved food additive under 21 CFR 172.831 (not GRAS).
EFSA exposure modeling identified possible ADI exceedance in high-end toddler scenarios.
Recent PubMed literature reports microbiome/glucose-homeostasis changes and impurity-related mechanistic concerns.
